# Carmel freight brokerage company opens new headquarters 

 By Piper Bailey on September 4, 2026 Carmel Business Local 

Since opening in Carmel in 2019, Koola Logistics has grown from three to approximately 100 employees. 

On Aug. 28, it celebrated its move into a new headquarters on the fifth floor of Hamilton Crossing VI with a ribbon-cutting ceremony. 

The facility is in a 38,000-square-foot space with offices, conference rooms, collaboration areas and more than 300 workstations to accommodate future growth. Employees also have access to building amenities, including a fitness center with showers, a café and lounge.

“Our roots are here in Carmel, and as we looked at what the next chapter of Koola Logistics should look like, we wanted to continue investing right here in this community,” stated Steve Paliska, Koola Logistics president and founder. “We’ve been fortunate to experience tremendous growth, but we still believe we are just getting started. This headquarters gives us the ability to continue building our team, creating jobs and growing Koola Logistics in Carmel for years to come.”

results.title: MyFreightWorld Expands in West Palm Beach, Adding 41 Jobs
results.text:
MyFreightWorld Expands in West Palm Beach, Adding 41 Jobs

# National Logistics Company to Expand West Palm Beach Operations

August 26, 2026 – West Palm Beach, FL – The Business Development Board of the Palm Beaches today announced the expansion of MyFreightWorld, a national third-party logistics company in West Palm Beach. The company will add 41 new team members over the next few years at an average income of $94,000. MyFreightWorld will move from its current location at 400 Clematis Street, Suite 203, into a 7,296-square-foot suite at 2090 Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard in West Palm Beach. The larger space is designed to support the company’s rapid growth and increased shipment activity across Palm Beach County and the country where it currently manages 25,000 shipments annually.

As it grows its current workforce from 20 to a total of 61 employees, the new positions are primarily for Account Executives and Account Management. Palm Beach County residents can apply online.

About the Expansion:

- Jobs: 41 new jobs in West Palm Beach; 20 current employees
- Pay: $94,000 average income
- Types of new roles: Account Executives, Account Management
- Link to apply: https://www.myfreight

# Opening a New Branch? How to Build Your First Team Without Costly Hiring Mistakes

21 Sept, 2026 8 Minutes

 

 By Freight Appointments 

Key takeaways

- Hire in phases. The Branch Manager comes first, then core operations by mode, and sales only once the branch can deliver.
- Settle licences and security approvals before you recruit the people who depend on them, especially for customs brokerage and air cargo.
- Branches outside the major freight hubs often need candidates willing to relocate, so build that into the search and the package.
- Freight Appointments recruits whole branch teams, from Branch Manager to entry writer, and only in freight forwarding.

Your reason for opening decides who you need first. Most forwarders open a new branch for one of four reasons.

# King of Freight Expands to Colorado Springs, Creating New Job Opportunities

Tuesday, 22 September 2026 04:10 PM

#### Company Update

Wichita-Based Logistics Company Opens New Office, Plans to Hire 100 Employees by End of 2026

WICHITA, KS / ACCESS Newswire / September 22, 2026 / King of Freight, a Wichita, Kansas-based logistics company, is expanding its footprint with a new office opening today in Colorado Springs, Colorado, creating new job opportunities in the region.

The new location marks a significant step in King of Freight's growth strategy, with the company aiming to hire 100 employees at the Colorado Springs office by the end of 2026. The expansion reflects continued demand for the company's logistics and freight services beyond its Kansas home base.

"Opening our Colorado Springs office is about more than growing our footprint. It's about bringing new job opportunities to a new community. We're excited to build a strong local team here and continue the same commitment to our people that has driven our growth from the start," said a King of Freight spokesperson.

GXO Logistics, Inc. is opening a regional office at T3 FAT Village in Fort Lauderdale, choosing Broward County for a company that ranks among the largest logistics providers in the world.

The move caps a yearlong recruiting effort led by The Greater Fort Lauderdale Alliance, a Workshop partner. It lands at T3, the centerpiece of the $500 million FAT Village redevelopment, co-developed by Urban Street Development, the Fort Lauderdale firm co-founded by Workshop members Tim Petrillo and Alan Hooper.

A company of this scale choosing Broward reflects the depth of the county's logistics infrastructure and talent, the kind of anchor move that draws others to follow.
